gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-arabic: Noto Sans Arabic opens its small letters wide and stands up high on the line, while Nordic huddles its shapes shut like folded leaves. Pure contrast, and the whole point.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-armenian: Noto Sans Armenian fills its round letters with generous, inviting space, giving the page a friendly, businesslike face. Nordic, by contrast, draws a bent-paperclip line that never swells or thins, and it feels ancient and powerful.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-avestan: Nordic keeps every horizontal as heavy as its verticals and closes its letters tight, like a stamped old seal. Noto Sans Avestan lets its curves stop short of touching, so text feels light and modern.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-buginese: Powerful and ancient, Nordic spaces its closed letters out like brush dabs, with a w that never thickens or thins. Big and short is where it belongs, over Noto Sans Buginese.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-buhid: Blunt, stamped, ancient: Nordic makes its horizontals exactly as heavy as its verticals and tucks each opening shut. And Noto Sans Buhid, with curve ends held well away from the stem, reads like a modern, professional sheet of paragraphs without any strain.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-cham: Nordic is all pressed-leaf folds and far-flung brush dabs, closed up and ancient. And Noto Sans Cham, with its wide-mouthed c and rounded, lofty lowercase, keeps paragraphs clean and modern from line to line.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-cherokee: Nordic looks like carved, unshaded strokes, powerful and old. Noto Sans Cherokee sits beneath it with a lofty band of lowercase and an e that gapes at the end, so the heavy, closed heading and the open, approachable text trade off smoothly.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-deseret: Noto Sans Deseret keeps its apertures open and its lowercase wide and high, with squat ascenders, which feels friendly and clean. And Nordic, closed and monoweight, belongs up big on a short line.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-devanagar: Powerful, with thin joins as thick as its stems, Nordic is the ancient half of this pair. And Noto Sans Devanagari, with an open-bowled g and capitals that melt into lowercase, brings a modern, even-keeled counterpoint beneath it.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-ethiopic: Noto Sans Ethiopic hangs its c terminals far from the bowl. Over a long page it stays sturdy, modern and businesslike, a stark contrast with Nordic's closed, flat-lined, ancient heading.
